title: Condensate Extraction Pump

introduction.definition: A condensate extraction pump (CEP) removes condensate from the condenser hotwell, which is under vacuum and at saturation, and pumps it through the low-pressure heaters to the deaerator. Because NPSH available is very low, it is a vertical can pump (VS6) whose first-stage impeller sits deep below the hotwell level.
applications: Steam power plants and combined-cycle plants
key_points: Can vent line back to condenser

classification.application: Power plant condensate system (typically 2 x 100 % or 3 x 50 % pumps)

introduction.summary: Condensate extraction pumps take condensed steam from the turbine condenser hotwell and push it through the low-pressure feedwater heaters to the deaerator. The liquid is saturated and under vacuum, so the NPSH available is very small; the pump is therefore a vertical can (barrel) pump whose first stage sits deep below the hotwell, gaining submergence. The can is vented back to the condenser so vapour cannot collect, and a minimum-flow line returns condensate to the condenser at low load.

video_tutorials.title: Condensate Extraction Pump — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Condensate Extraction Pump.
A condensate extraction pump (CEP) removes condensate from the condenser hotwell, which is under vacuum and at saturation, and pumps it through the low-pressure heaters to the deaerator.
Because NPSH available is very low, it is a vertical can pump (VS6) whose first-stage impeller sits deep below the hotwell level.
Typical applications include steam power plants and combined-cycle plants; industrial turbine condensers (alumina, sugar, paper).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Discharge Case (Top Bowl), Bowl – Stage 1, Bowl Wear Ring – Stage 1, Impeller – Stage 1.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.

video_tutorials.title: Condensate Extraction Pump — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Condensate Extraction Pump.
Check seal water and vibration.
Check vent line.
Inspect first stage.
Watch for air in-leakage: dissolved oxygen rise. Common cause: gland leaking under vacuum.
Watch for first-stage cavitation: noise. Common cause: low hotwell level.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
